thread.title: How High Can Apple Stock Go? This Analyst Says the Sky's the Limit

title: How High Can Apple Stock Go? This Analyst Says the Sky's the Limit
text:
How High Can Apple Stock Go? This Analyst Says the Sky’s the Limit By Oct. 19, 2018 10:23 a.m. ET Order Reprints Apple's Steve Jobs Theater in Cupertino, California Noah Berger/AFP/Getty Images Text size
The sky’s the limit for Apple (AAPL), Wedbush Securities analyst Daniel Ives said in a note late Thursday that gave the company the highest price target on Wall Street.
How high? In his Overweight recommendation, Ives, managing director of equity research, initiated coverage with a $310 target on the stock, a 43.5% upside from Thursday’s closing price. He boldly predicted Apple will reach about $1.5 trillion in market value within 18 months.
Insatiable demand for Apple’s new crop of iPhones, including its highest-priced model yet (the $1,099 iPhone XS Max), will lead the charge in 2019 and beyond, Ives told Barron’s .
“We expect big things out of Apple,” he said.
In his note, Ives said a whopping 350 million iPhones are in the “window of opportunity” to upgrade in the next 12-18 months, “with Apple needing to capture a majority of these units as part of this upgrade cycle to make a clearly successful iPhone product cycle in 2019 and lay the groundwork” for future growth. Newsletter Sign-up
Price points and features of the trio of new iPhones launched in September—which also included the iPhone XS and iPhone XR—will be more appealing to consumers who bypassed the iPhone 8/iPhone 8 Plus/iPhone X cycle a year earlier, Ives said. So much so, he said, that they will break through among Chinese consumers.
Strong iPhone sales, in turn, will further ignite the “high octane fuel” that is Apple’s services business, Ives said, who forecasts $50 billion in annual revenue by 2020.
“In a nutshell, we ultimately believe [Apple’s] valuation can approach the $1.5 trillion level,” Ives wrote.
Through Thursday, 26 analysts had Buy recommendations on Apple stock (13 were Hold and one Sell), with a mean price target of $239.02, according to FactSet . The company is scheduled to announce fiscal fourth-quarter earnings on Nov. 1, the first quarter in which sales of its new iPhones are reported.
